derived_from: src/tooluniverse/agentic_tool.py -- AgenticTool.run has exactly six returns: three for configs.return_metadata true (tool unavailable, success, exception) and three for false (a plain error string, the model's answer itself, format_error_response).

src/tooluniverse/llm_clients.py -- infer(...) -> Optional[str]. With no custom_format it returns resp.choices[0].message.content, and None once max_retries is spent. return_json only asks the API for JSON *mode*; the JSON comes back as unparsed text. GeminiClient.infer says the same in prose: 'Both hand back an unparsed JSON string.'
how: These payloads are DERIVED FROM SOURCE, not measured live. Every AgenticTool is skipped at load time when no LLM API key is present (execute_function.py checks AgenticTool.has_any_api_keys before registering one), so no call could be made here and the error branches are not reachable through tu.run either. The derivation is exhaustive instead of a lower bound, which a live pass would not have been: run() has six returns and this file covers all six. What a live pass WOULD add is whether a given model honours its prompt's requested JSON shape -- which is why no declaration in this change narrows `result` beyond the type the client guarantees, and why the shapes the prompts ask for are described in prose or carried in an annotation-only contentSchema rather than asserted.
the_trap: configs.return_json true does NOT mean `result` is a parsed object. 23 of these tools declared type object on that assumption. The project's own consumers get it right -- compose_scripts/tool_discover.py and tool_description_optimizer.py take obj['result'], check isinstance(str) and json.loads it -- so the code and the declarations disagreed, and only the declarations were wrong.
invariant: every payload here validates against its tool's return_schema, and exactly one oneOf branch matches it; every payload under unreachable validates against none
